update.title: M09 humility: 10.14 Humility written, angles woven into their chapters, four corrections
update.researcher_instruction: "excellent work.  bring the narrative up to date, and ensure that the claims register / narrative is updated" (2026-10-15); placement: "Your recommendation. Ch 14 might expand in scope as we move forward, but it needs its own chapter to encapsulate it properly.  It does have many different  angles that need to be woven onto those chapters in context of each angle."; "humility is not a feeling"; "Jesus is part of divinity and need attention in Ch 13"
update.method: Humbling oneself fanned out across clusters (218 verses: the M09 words and the humility, meekness, contrite and submission words filed in M05, M10, M23, M24, M53, M73, M75, T2, T3), read in five batches by passage; the 27 no-other-M-code verses read; OT/NT comparison and the role of Jesus; cross-check against the narrative, register, M08 and M47. New 10.14 Humility holds the full account; each angle woven into its chapter in context (10.2, 10.7, 10.9, 10.10, Ch 4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13.1), pointers in 10.1, 10.12, 10.13, 10.0. Cross-check corrections: Ch 12 "weighed most" (uncounted superlative removed); Mic 6:8 taken out of the anger-at-wrong-to-the-weak statements in 10.8 and 10.13 and placed for what it says; Ch 11 "rest that passes from his heart to ours" restated to the verse; Ch 14 held bullet "seven conditions for the Spirit's work" (2Ch 7:14) removed, the verse now told in 10.14, claim 10-5 withdrawn. Correction 5 (claim 1-1 sources) needs no change: the claim was widened to heart // spirit on first record.
update.not_woven_note: The poor and needy are carried by threads OT-105 (the poor as seen by another) and OT-106 (the poor person's own side), not woven. The serve/servant words (Mar 10:45; Joh 13; 2Cor 8:9) were not pulled. Ch 1 outline (#2111) not touched.
update.structure_change: New sub-chapter 10.14 Humility (reading order after 10.13). New sections: 10.2 Humility and hearing; 10.7 Taking the lower place; 10.9 Humbling oneself before God; 10.10 Humility toward one another; Ch 4 The heart humbled; Ch 5 Rest for the soul; 13.1 Lowering himself. Ch 6 gains a paragraph (It is gentle, and it is under the person); Ch 11 s4 a face (Who lowers whom, and before whom); Ch 12 the counterpart paragraph. 10.0 names 10.12 to 10.14.
update.structure_reason: Humility is not a feeling (researcher); the readings show it as act, standing, sought quality, state of spirit, place taken, done to a person and God's own way, across the activities. A key characteristic gets one full account as its own Ch 10 sub-chapter (#1961), with each angle woven in context (#1920).
update.quote_note: every quoted part in the added lines of the 17 files checked against iba.db verse text in chapter order, case-insensitive (capitals at the start of a quote only)
update.notes: The 10.14 chapter row was added directly to narrative_chapter (reading_order 25, later chapters +1) because no Narrative-Register action adds a chapter.

passages.anchor: The seven conditions for the Spirit's work

new.text: Humility is not a feeling in the verses; they speak of it as an act, a standing, a quality sought and walked in, a state of the spirit, a place taken, something done to a person, and God's own way
new.beyond_text: gathers the faces of humility across the humbling words; no verse read says a person feels humble

new.text: Humility is always set against a rising: the proud heart, the lifted-up self, the stiff neck, the haughty eyes
new.beyond_text: reads the opposite named beside humbling in every face as one setting

new.text: Humbling oneself is done before someone: God, or the prophet who carries his word
new.beyond_text: joins the "before" of each account; reads Zedekiah's refusal of the prophet as refusal of the word

new.text: Most often a person humbles himself when a word reaches him, and the humbling owns that God is right
new.beyond_text: counts the accounts in which a word comes first; reads "The Lord is righteous" as what the humbling says

new.text: Humbling happens in the heart; Hezekiah's is the same heart turning back from its own pride
new.beyond_text: places the act in the heart from the heart named in each verse; reads 2Ch 32:25-26 as one heart in two directions

new.text: The one who exalts himself measures himself against others and lists what he does; the one who humbles himself owns that he is a sinner and asks for mercy
new.beyond_text: reads the two prayers of the parable as the two acts

new.text: To humble oneself under God's hand is also to put down what one carries, because he cares; the lifting is his to time
new.beyond_text: joins humbling and casting anxieties in 1Pe 5:6-7 as one act

new.text: Distress does not decide whether a person humbles himself; the same pressure or call meets two hearts, and the verses do not say why
new.beyond_text: sets Manasseh beside Ahaz and the scorners beside those who came

new.text: God sees the one who humbles himself and answers, in measure; the humbling does not hold by itself
new.beyond_text: gathers the seeing, the measured answers and Rehoboam's relapse

new.text: The humbling God does not take knowledge of is kept alongside self-pleasure and oppression and leaves the seen naked uncovered; Ahab's, against himself when the word came, was answered
new.beyond_text: compares Isa 58 with 1Ki 21 and reads the difference in what goes with the acts

new.text: What looks like lowering can puff a person up
new.beyond_text: reads the humility noun as "asceticism" in Col 2 beside the Pharisee's fasting

new.text: God humbles to show what is in the heart, to teach what a person lives by, and to do him good in the end, against the heart that lifts itself up in plenty
new.beyond_text: gathers the stated purposes of God's humbling

new.text: Being humbled by God can turn a person or harden him
new.beyond_text: sets Ahaz beside Manasseh

new.text: What God brings low is a bearing, haughty looks and lofty pride, not only a rank, so that the Lord alone is exalted
new.beyond_text: reads the objects named in the bringing low as a bearing

new.text: Only God lifts up and puts down; a person cannot abase the proud
new.beyond_text: joins the challenge to Job with Psa 75

new.text: The boast is moved from what a person has to what God does
new.beyond_text: reads Jam 1:9-10 and 1Co 1:28-31 together

new.text: Humility is not held once for all: the humble are told to seek it
new.beyond_text: reads "all you humble … seek humility"

new.text: The humble are glad at what God did for another
new.beyond_text: reads both psalms as one man's rescue made others' gladness

new.text: The humble are the teachable, and the teachable own their guilt
new.beyond_text: reads Psa 25:9 with the speaker's own prayer for pardon

new.text: Meekness stands where another provokes and leaves the answer to God
new.beyond_text: reads Psa 37 and Num 12 together

new.text: Humility goes with the ear that can take a reproof and a word, and does not answer before it hears
new.beyond_text: reads the verses set beside "humility comes before honor" as one

new.text: In four passages what God looks to is set against a religious act; the offering follows the broken heart
new.beyond_text: counts the four passages; reads Psa 51:19 as the offering following

new.text: Where God and a broken heart meet he is near and heals; the verses tell the breaking by its cause and by whether it is brought to God, not by naming contrition or despair
new.beyond_text: gathers the broken-heart verses by cause and outcome

new.text: Humility between people is a way of counting the other, worn toward them, and named with bearing with and forgiving
new.beyond_text: gathers the humility-toward-one-another verses

new.text: The lower place is taken before anyone gives it; the honour is given, not taken
new.beyond_text: reads the seat, the title and the child together

new.text: Gentleness in meeting a wrong is joined to watching oneself, remembering what one was, and leaving the outcome to God
new.beyond_text: gathers what the gentleness verses join to it

new.text: Submitting to God and humbling oneself are said as one
new.beyond_text: reads Jam 4:7-10 as one run

new.text: Submission among people is told with a ground that faces God and, where the passage goes on, with a duty on the other side
new.beyond_text: counts the grounds and the paired duties

new.text: Refusing submission is right where the truth of the gospel is at stake
new.beyond_text: reads Gal 2:5 as the limit

new.text: One's own spirit is under the person: the one who speaks governs what moves in him
new.beyond_text: reads 1Co 14:32 as submission inward

new.text: In the New Testament humility rests on what is said of Jesus; the saying he taught, that whoever humbles himself will be exalted, is what is told of him
new.beyond_text: ties Phi 2:8-9 and Heb 2:9 back to the saying in the Gospels

new.text: Jesus is given as the ground and example of humility toward others
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses that name him as the ground

new.text: John's lowering of himself before Jesus is said with joy
new.beyond_text: reads Joh 3:30 with 3:28-29

new.text: The same lines of humility run through both Testaments; the New differs in emphasis, adding humility toward one another, and in one new thing, Christ, in whom God's lowering is done in a human life
new.beyond_text: compares the readings of the two Testaments

new.text: Humility changes character with who acts, toward whom, and to what end
new.beyond_text: sets the faces of the same words side by side

new.text: The lowering that the Old Testament tells of God is done in the Son in a human life
new.beyond_text: reads God's looking down, dwelling with the lowly, gentleness and being broken beside the Son's emptying and humbling

new.text: God sees and answers the one who humbles himself, gives favor to the humble, humbles to test and do good, brings the proud low and looks on a humble estate
new.beyond_text: gathers God's acts toward the humble and the proud

edit.note: 2Ch 7:14 read in the M09 humbling fan-out (#2148, batch 1): the verse names humbling, prayer, seeking his face and turning, and God hearing, forgiving and healing; it names no Spirit and no count of seven.
